answer: Graph-based trust propagation curbs Sybil attacks by routing interaction rights through transitive attestations from trusted seed identities. In decentralized networks spanning an orchard, a tundra, or a pearl hatchery, agents accept requests only along verified topological paths. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of convincing authentic peers to sign unforgeable trust endorsements. However, this mechanism marginalizes newly initialized agents that lack established connections.
